analysis.title: Global Rates Weekly: Red, wiped, and blue
key_insights: BofA's US pay 2Y trade hit its stop and closed on 6 Nov 2026 (entry 4.73%, stop 4.45%, target 5.25%). The trade was opened after the hawkish Sept FOMC and was well in the money in late Sept, then reversed on a dovish Fed, tech weakness and the oil drop. BofA keeps an underweight front end (pay) bias with reduced conviction.

US rates fell with the 5Y outperforming on the curve. Oil fell about 15% w/w amid post-election speculation on Iran de-escalation, with a sharp risk-off led by tech. Commodity-sensitive rates led the global bull steepening.

The 'blue sweep' (Democratic midterm sweep) reinforces BofA's gridlock base case. Democrats lack a veto-proof Senate majority. The bigger near-term risk is state and local regulation of data centers, which could make the AI buildout slower and more expensive. BofA calls the sweep a headwind to its pay front end and curve flattening views, though unlikely to matter near term.

Consensus is centered on Iran de-escalation, peak global growth, and a well-priced central bank cycle. BofA leans contrarian on all three: de-escalation is far from certain, the growth tailwind is weaker near term but more persistent medium term, and the shallow central bank path is not fixed.

BofA economists expect Oct NFP of +75k (Bloomberg consensus 65k, Sept 29k) and a stable 4.2% unemployment rate, with risk of 4.1%. A 0.1ppt move in the u-rate would move the 2Y by 5-7bp. Oct CPI m/m expectation is core 0.23% and headline 0.18%, with risks skewed higher after two months of upside surprises. A 0.3% core print would raise pressure on the Fed.

The November refunding kept coupon auction sizes unchanged. Treasury changed forward guidance to 'for the next several quarters', dropping 'at least'. BofA reads this as no size changes for 3-5 quarters. Treasury ignored the TBAC recommendation to raise coupon sizes in 2H FY27.

BofA moves its forecast for coupon auction size increases from Aug '27 to Nov '27 because of debt limit dynamics. Increases would span 2y-10y with most growth in 2y-5y, keeping bills near 25% of marketable debt. BofA flags that its front-end auction size projections look outsized relative to GDP.
BofA stays long 30Y asset swap spreads post refunding, citing Treasury and TBAC focus on balancing supply and demand and on taxpayer cost. It expects the theme to remain supportive in 2027.

The US debt limit is now likely to bind as early as Feb '27, with Treasury debt subject to the limit $557bn below the $41.1tn ceiling. BofA keeps its X-date forecast at Nov '27 but sees Treasury uncomfortably close by mid Aug '27. Higher bill supply raises the TGA minimum and reduces debt limit flexibility.

Debt limit episodes usually bring easier funding conditions because the TGA falls and reserves rise. BofA likes long M7 3m SOFR/FF (current -2.4bp, target 0, stop -5bp), with early debt limit resolution as the risk. A Fed 'sterilization' of TGA outflows is a non-base-case risk, with up to $700bn offsettable in Feb.

Europe: BofA estimates 10y OAT-Bund (currently 155bp) ranges from about 75bp in an optimistic case (1y1y at 2.5%, spread decoupled from risk assets) to just over 250bp in a negative case (spread decoupled from rates, equities down 10%). The ECB's pain threshold is seen as much higher than the market's, and TPI is seen as the distant backstop.

Europe: BofA leans bullish duration in the belly. With 1y1y €str at 3% (two hikes priced), it sees better risk-reward in receiving 2y2y or 3y2y, also at 3%. In past episodes with 1y1y at 3%, 2y2y traded lower (2.8% in Oct-23 and Sep-22, 2.5% in Dec-22).

UK: the BoE hiked 25bp on 5 Nov with an 8-1 vote (one vote for 50bp). The hike was more hawkish than BofA expected, with the inflation peak revised up to 4.9% in Q2 2027 and Lombardelli and Pill opening the door to near-term action. Dovish elements included medium-term inflation at 1.8%, limited evidence of second-round effects, and Bailey saying this is not the start of an inevitable long sequence.

BofA still expects a second BoE hike to 4.25% in February, but December risk has risen and a third hike is possible. It sees market pricing of four total hikes as excessive and 13bp priced for December as reasonable. The MPC-dated Sonia strip rose 6.5bp on average. BofA holds receive June 2027 MPC-dated Sonia (entry 4.72%, target 4.41%, stop 4.86%, current 4.58%) and the 1y fwd 2s10s Sonia steepener (entry 13.9bp, target 45bp, stop 0bp, current 8.8bp).

UK supply: next Tuesday's £1bn auction of the 5⅜% Gilt 2056 begins the DMO's task of raising more than £10bn from longs in the final five months of the fiscal year, against under £5bn raised so far. Supply indigestion could add bear-steepening pressure.

Australia: the RBA hiked on a split 6-3 vote, which BofA calls an insurance hike at the cycle peak, after 125bp of cumulative hikes in 2026. BofA sees a very low chance of further hikes and reluctance to hike before at least Q2 '27, with high conviction that the next move is a cut. It recommends U7/U8 bill flatteners (entry -23bp, target -50bp, stop -6bp), which roll at 7bp per quarter. Risk is a strong Oct CPI print.
BofA expects AU rates, particularly the belly, to outperform US rates over 3-12 months as policy diverges, with the Fed seen continuing to hike into 2027.

Technicals: the US 10Y yield is testing the uptrend line from the March low at about 4.83%. BofA's bias since Nov 2025 has been to pay rates and this is a level to consider paying, but an unorthodox head-and-shoulders top and risk-off limit conviction. A break above the right-shoulder high at 5.05% would invalidate the pattern risk, and below 4.73% the cyclical pay view is in doubt.

Trade book changes this week: closed short 2y UST at 4.45%, opened U7 vs U8 flatteners at -23bp. Other open themes include 2s30s flattener (entry 62bp, latest 80bp, stop 100bp), 5s30s CA swaps flattener vs US, long 10y20y inflation swap, long 2y and 30y ASW, and receive June 2027 MPC-dated Sonia.

BofA forecasts (YE26): Fed funds 4.125%, 10y UST 5.00%, ECB refi 2.90%, 10y Bund 3.40%, BoJ 1.50%, 10y JGB 3.00%, BoE 4.00%, 10y gilt 5.20%, RBA 4.60%, 10y ACGB 5.15%, 10y Canada 4.00%. BofA's forecasts are more hawkish than market pricing in the US, EU and Japan. It expects two more Fed hikes in Dec '26 and Mar '27.

risk_factors: Equity risk-off, including a tech melt and possible capex slowdown from data center regulation or hyperscaler restraint.
Oil price swings tied to the Iran conflict, with Europe more sensitive to oil down days than the US.
Strong October US CPI (core 0.3% m/m) raising Fed pressure, and the NFP surprise risk.
Debt limit binding as early as Feb '27 with X-date risk by mid Aug '27, and a possible Fed sterilization of TGA outflows.
Weak JGB auctions (30Y on Nov 10, 5Y on Nov 12) and fiscal news from the Diet session.
UK fiscal and supply risk from a long gilt debt raise, plus a hawkish BoE and a possible December hike.
French affordability protests widening OAT-Bund spreads, with a distant ECB TPI backstop.
A US 10Y head-and-shoulders top with a 5.05% invalidation level, and a break below 4.73% putting the cyclical pay view in doubt.
Strong Australian October CPI undermining the U7/U8 flattener.
charts_described: Exhibit 8 plots the initial NFP print vs Bloomberg consensus gap against the day's 2Y UST move since 2023, with a fit of y = 0.0652x - 0.6141 and R² = 0.2285.
Exhibit 9 shows 10y OAT-Bund fair values by regression: with 1y1y at 2.5%, 71-137bp, and with 1y1y at 3% and SX5E 10% lower, 89-255bp.
Exhibit 21 compares Bloomberg's UK Government Securities Liquidity Index with BofA proxies, with excluding low coupon bonds producing a clear downward level shift.
vol_and_positioning: BofA holds a long forward vol bias in the US (short left vs right vol), with open trades short 1y1y vs 1y10y vol and 2s10s floor ladders. It also holds 15m1y vs 3m1y receiver calendars.
Europe: vol is supported into YE26 on ECB uncertainty and lower in 2027, via a long 3m2y rec 1x2 and a short 3m2y EU vs US vol trade (entry 8-Oct-26 at +4bp/v, latest 23bp/v).
Japan: vol supported and outperforming other DM markets (short 6m1y 1x2).
Australia: vol supported near term and lower medium term, led by the left side via receiver calendars.
Moves in the US 2Y: BofA estimates a 0.1ppt change in the unemployment rate leads to a 5-7bp move, and a roughly 100k NFP miss implies about +/-5bp on the 10Y.
geopolitical: Iran de-escalation speculation after the US midterm election drove oil about 15% lower w/w. BofA says de-escalation is far from certain.
US-Iran war outlook is still uncertain, which BofA cites as a reason for the ECB and rates outlook uncertainty and for the BoE's energy price assumptions.
US midterms produced a Democratic sweep (blue wave), reinforcing a gridlock base case, with risk of tighter state and local data-center regulation.
French protests over affordability are flagged as a focus for the week ahead, along with a UK gilt long-end debt raise.
The BoE said further hikes are unlikely to be the last unless the Iran conflict is resolved.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus sees Iran de-escalation, lower oil and a well-priced central bank cycle supporting a shallow path and falling yields.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA argues de-escalation is far from certain, the growth tailwind is more persistent medium term, and the shallow central bank path is not fixed, so the front end can reprice higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close below the 4.83% trend line reduces BofA's pay-rates conviction, and below 4.73% the cyclical pay view is in doubt.

tension_points.bull_case: Market prices four total hikes, with a hawkish 8-1 vote, a raised 4.9% inflation peak and near-term language from Lombardelli and Pill.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA sees limited second-round effects, lower energy futures than the MPC baseline and soft labour markets, so only two hikes are likely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Strong second-round effects actually materializing, or higher energy prices or upside data surprises, would make a December hike live and support more than two hikes.

tension_points.theme: US front end pay bias vs risk-off
tension_points.bull_case: Solid growth, stable labor market, resilient consumer, sticky inflation and geopolitical risk support paying the front end and flattening curves.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk-off, the oil drop, a Democratic sweep, possible AI capex slowdown and a head-and-shoulders top in the 10Y weigh on the pay view.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print of 0.3% m/m would raise Fed pressure, supporting the view. Failure would come from a more significant tightening of financial conditions or clearer growth impact from AI/hyperscaler restraint.

theme_stances.key_argument: Solid growth, sticky inflation and a stable labor market support an underweight front end bias despite the stop-out.
The BoE's signal was about the timing of the next hike, not a higher terminal rate, and four hikes are excessive.
theme_stances.evidence: the key signal from the BoE was about the timing and sequencing of the next hike
